brief.title: Q3 board update
brief.goal: Approve two more support engineers before October.
brief.audience: Five board members who think support costs are already too high.
brief.bigIdea: Two support hires now cut churn faster than any product change.

points.text: Churn rose after ticket wait times doubled
points.example: Churn went from 3% to 7% in one quarter

points.text: Hiring is cheaper than lost revenue
points.example: Two hires cost $240k and churn cost $900k

brief.openingLine: We lost 41 customers this quarter, and 30 of them waited over two days for support.
brief.closingLine: Approve two support hires today, and we cut churn before the holiday renewals.

issues.problem: The big idea claims hires beat any product change, but no point compares hiring speed or cost to a product fix.
issues.action: Add a point that shows how long a product fix would take and what it would cost, then compare it to the hires.

issues.problem: The board already believes support costs are too high, but the points only compare hire cost to churn loss, not to the current budget.
issues.action: Add a line showing support spend as a share of revenue to show the raise is small next to the risk.
